Xi Is Getting What He Wants
items.description: Once Upon a Time in the Middle East , a movie that premiered in China last month and is coming to the United States in October, is about a Chinese chef who moves to the Middle East to find work, only to become a savior for the locals amid the chaos of an American invasion. This box-office hit has earned rave reviews in China—especially from China’s government, which has promoted the film’s themes of Chinese peacefulness versus American warmongering. The film “casts US as invader, outperforms Hollywood,” according to a headline from the Global Times , a news outlet run by the Communist Party. The message: America is the bad guy, and China’s job is to clean up. Donald Trump should keep that in mind as Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for his first state visit since 2015. Trump may laud Xi as a respected friend, as he did when the two men met in Beijing in May. Yet Xi is no friend of Trump’s. Throughout his 14 years in power, China’s president has acted deliberately and consistently to undermine the United States. His two-day trip to Washington now seems perfectly timed to exploit the weakness of his host and main strategic rival, lately enfeebled by rising domestic prices, plummeting approval ratings, and a costly ongoing war in Iran. This timing makes the spectacle of the purported leader of the free world fawning over a Communist dictator more than just embarrassing. Trump’s soft touch on China is widely unpopular in Washington. In advance of a summit that is expected to cover AI safety, trade, and Taiwan, John Moolenaar, the chair ​of the House Select Committee on China and a member of the U.S. president’s own Republican Party, called for a tougher line. Xi, mindful that American foreign policy can change dramatically with elections, seems to see the Trump administration as a potentially brief window of opportunity to expand Chinese influence. While Trump has been distracted by the Iran war and White House redecorations, Xi has remained focused on enhancing China’s technological and industrial might and diplomatically asserting Beijing’s global leadership. In the weeks before this visit, Xi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at two major forums for developing countries, where he pitched China as a more stable and reliable great power than the United States. Although Xi avoids mentioning the U.S. by name, he leaves little doubt which country he is describing as a rogue state that threatens global peace. “Unilateralism and power politics are surging against the tide,” Xi told the BRICS group of emerging economies, which includes Brazil, Russia, India, and China, earlier this month, “lashing at multilateralism and the international order.” [ Read: China is flatlining ] Xi seems to perceive himself as a man of destiny, ruling China at a pivotal moment when he can build and lead a new world order. “Today, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world,” he said in that BRICS speech, repeating a phrase he often uses to describe global shifts in the balance of power. “The global South is gaining strength, and the trend toward a multipolar world is unstoppable,” he declared. Xi’s “whole worldview is to see a new international order arise where China and authoritarian states play a bigger role,” Nicholas Burns, a former U.S. ambassador to China who is now a professor of diplomacy at Harvard University, told me. Xi’s “short- and long-term view is that we’re standing in China’s way as China seeks to become more influential, more powerful in the world,” he added, referring to the United States. But, if Beijing is right, it won’t be for much longer. Xi and others in China’s elite believe that the U.S. is in decline. Wang Huning, the Communist Party’s chief theorist and a close adviser to Xi, helped shape this assumption with America Against America , a 1991 book about his travels in the U.S., in which he portrayed the country as rich and technologically advanced but rotting from within due to its eroding public institutions and decaying cultural values. Rather than waiting patiently for the U.S. to fall apart on its own, Xi has spent his entire reign testing the pillars of American power. In 2013, he launched the Belt and Road Initiative, a global infrastructure-building program to expand China’s influence in the developing world. In 2015, he introduced the “Made in China 2025” program, a plan to dominate various manufacturing industries, such as electric vehicles, through massive state support. Against Washington’s objections, Xi has asserted China’s claims to the South China Sea by building military installations in the vital waterway. Since 2021, he has promoted a series of “global initiatives” to spread his vision of a reformed world order based on Chinese political principles. In 2022, he deepened his partnership with Putin days before the Russian leader invaded Ukraine. Yet even though Xi has worked hard to reduce China’s reliance on the United States by developing homegrown technology, promoting the Chinese currency in global business, and expanding trade with the developing world, China’s economy still exchanged more than $410 billion in goods with America last year—and depends on the economic stability of the U.S. for its own growth. Rather than take the United States head-on, as the Soviet Union tried to do during the Cold War, Xi has worked to carefully undermine American power without provoking a costly confrontation. During Trump’s visit to Beijing in May, Xi asked whether the two countries could avoid the Thucydides Trap—the theory that an established power will invariably clash with a rising one, owing to the threat of being displaced. Trump seemed to miss the point. In a post on Truth Social a day later, he implied that his America was under no such threat: “When President Xi very elegantly referred to the United States as perhaps being a declining nation, he was referring to the tremendous damage we suffered during the four years of Sleepy Joe Biden and the Biden Administration, and on that score, he was 100% correct.” But in posing his question, Xi was signaling why he bothers meeting with Trump. Xi “believes that the United States, despite its descent in global politics, still is enormously potentially dangerous,” Kurt Campbell, a former U.S. deputy secretary of state and now the chair of the Asia Group, a consulting firm, told me. “Xi is animated by the idea of how to avoid a great-power war and to help ease the United States into a more orderly decline. He believes that this kind of personal diplomacy with Trump is an important ingredient” in that strategy. [ Listen: Trump battles against an economy of his making ] So far, Xi’s approach has paid off. In return for spending a few hours with Trump, he has effectively neutralized his supposedly more powerful opponent. Trump appears to have little interest in pressuring Xi to step back from his partnership with Putin, even as it has likely sustained Moscow’s war in Ukraine. Despite threats to sanction countries that support Iran, the Trump administration has not taken meaningful action against China, Tehran’s largest oil customer. Trump has also softened American support for Taiwan, which Beijing claims as its own, including by delaying approval for a $14 billion arms sale to the democratically governed island. From Beijing’s perspective, Trump is simply bowing to the global shift in power. “It’s the reality of the world that China is rising, and the U.S. has to accept that,” Wang Huiyao, the president of the Center for China and Globalization, a Beijing-based think tank, told me. “We have to coexist, compromise, accommodate each other. That’s what Trump is doing.” In the United States, however, Trump’s dalliances with Xi look more like appeasement. Engaging in constructive dialogue to stabilize relations between the two great powers makes perfect sense, but Trump’s efforts seem to involve conceding to Xi’s wishes while avoiding the issues that matter most to American industry and security. Perhaps the midterm elections, now only weeks away, will deliver a new Congress capable of checking Trump’s behavior. But given the president’s personalized approach to China, anyone hoping for a smarter, tougher line on Beijing may have to wait for a new president—one who understands who the bad guy really is.

items.title: MP status does not place anyone beyond law – EOCO on Manhyia South MP’s attempted arrest
items.description: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has stressed that being a Member of Parliament does not, by itself, end an ongoing investigation or place an individual beyond the reach of the law. The statement follows the attempted arrest of Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, in connection with an ongoing investigation. EOCO said it was aware that the MP subsequently proceeded to the precincts of Parliament to seek sanctuary, although Parliament is currently on recess. The Office said it recognises and respects the constitutional privileges and immunities enjoyed by MPs and will ensure that its operations comply with the Constitution and applicable laws. “For the avoidance of doubt, Membership of Parliament does not, by itself, bring an investigation to an end or place an individual beyond the reach of the law,” EOCO said. The Office, however, stressed that its position does not mean it intends to disregard parliamentary privilege or other constitutional protections. “At the same time, EOCO will not take any step that is inconsistent with parliamentary privilege or any other protection provided by the Constitution,” it added. EOCO said its investigation remains active and that it will continue to discharge its statutory responsibilities while respecting the Constitution, the rule of law and parliamentary privileges.

items.title: Chief Justice must examine arrests of suspects on court premises – Afenyo-Markin
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has called on the Chief Justice to examine the practice of law enforcement agencies attempting to arrest suspects on court premises. His comments follow an alleged attempt by officers believed to be from the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) to arrest Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah after he appeared at the Accra High Court on Wednesday, September 23. Addressing a press conference in Parliament, Mr Afenyo-Markin said the alleged incident raises concerns about the conduct of investigating agencies within court premises. “Honourable Baffour is a lawyer by profession. Upon his account, he went to defend his client in court, then just after exiting the courtroom on the court premises, EOCO appeared there, laid an ambush and made an attempt to arrest him,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin said the Chief Justice should determine whether investigating agencies are permitted to enter court premises with the specific intention of arresting a suspect or accused person. “I think the justice delivery system, our Chief Justice, must look at this, whether or not EOCO or any investigating agency is allowed to enter court premises with the sole aim of accosting a suspect or an accused person. That must be looked at in context,” he said. The Minority Leader also raised concerns about what he described as a departure from the established procedure for state agencies seeking the presence of Members of Parliament. He explained that agencies such as the Office of the Special Prosecutor, the Ghana Police Service and EOCO are expected to formally write to the Speaker of Parliament when they require an MP to appear before an investigating body. According to him, the Speaker subsequently refers the request to Parliament’s leadership, which works with the legal directorate to make arrangements for the MP to avail himself. “There is nothing like preferential treatment, but because of the nature of the MP’s work, that procedure has been set in place, and that is what all state security agencies observe,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin therefore questioned the circumstances surrounding the alleged incident. “So the question is: what has changed?” he asked.

items.title: Lait infantile : une nouvelle usine de 10 000 tonnes lancée en Algérie
items.description: Une autre grande unité de production de lait infantile verra le jour en Algérie. Le chantier de la future usine a été inspecté ce mercredi 23 septembre à Larbatache, dans la wilaya de Boumerdès, par le directeur général de l'Agence algérienne de promotion de l’investissement (AAPI), Omar Rekkache. Cet investissement s’inscrit dans le cadre de la vision exprimée par le président de la République pour la production locale de ce produit que l'Algérie importe entièrement de l’étranger. Lait infantile : lancement d’une usine de 10.000 tonnes à Larbatache Selon les explications fournies par l’AAPI, cet investissement de la société privée Baby Infant Nutrition permettra de produire 5.000 tonnes de lait infantile par an dans un premier temps. La production sera ensuite portée progressivement à 10.000 tonnes. L’usine entrera en production en juillet 2027 et devrait générer 100 postes d’emplois directs. Un premier projet d’usine de lait infantile avait été lancé à Oran en juillet 2025. D’un investissement de 42 millions de dollars porté par la société Tazi, l’usine devrait avoir une capacité de production de 40 millions de boîtes de lait infantile par an, soit 40 % des besoins nationaux. Face à la hausse de la facture d’achat de ce produit stratégique et vital que l’Algérie importe à 100 %, le président Tebboune a appelé en juillet 2022 en Conseil des ministres à établir des partenariats pour fabriquer du lait infantile en Algérie. Des consultations ont été lancées par le ministère de l’Industrie en août de la même année. L’article Lait infantile : une nouvelle usine de 10 000 tonnes lancée en Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Black Stars arrive in Bouake ahead of Cote d’Ivoire clash
items.description: Ghana’s Black Stars have arrived in Bouake ahead of their opening 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Cote d’Ivoire on Thursday. The team travelled from Accra on Wednesday morning and arrived in the Ivorian city later in the day as preparations for the Group C opener entered the final stage. Head coach Carlos Queiroz is expected to lead the team through their final training session at the Stade de la Paix, the venue for Thursday’s game. The session will allow the players to familiarise themselves with the pitch, while Queiroz will have the opportunity to make his final tactical adjustments. The Black Stars opened camp in Accra on Monday and held their initial training sessions at the Accra Sports Stadium. Eighteen players trained on Tuesday as the squad continued to take shape following several withdrawals and late additions. Ghana have been hit by a number of absences ahead of the qualifier, with Mohammed Kudus, Antoine Semenyo and Nathaniel Adjei among those unavailable. Queiroz has responded by bringing in several replacements, including Osasuna defender Rockson Yeboah, who has received his first senior call-up after making three La Liga appearances this season. Thursday’s fixture will be Ghana’s first Group C match as the Black Stars begin their bid to return to the Africa Cup of Nations after missing the 2025 tournament in Morocco. The Black Stars will be hoping to leave Bouake with a positive result before returning home to face The Gambia on September 27. Cote d’Ivoire, Ghana, The Gambia and Somalia make up Group C, with the Black Stars looking to make a strong start under Queiroz. The Portuguese coach will be hoping his side can negotiate a difficult away fixture and return to Accra with a result to build momentum for the rest of the qualifying campaign.

According to EOCO in a statement, the two individuals were identified from a video of the incident that occurred on Wednesday, September 23, 2026. The Office said the conduct of the two persons is currently being assessed as part of its review of the incident. “EOCO has identified two persons who, based on the video, allegedly intervened to facilitate the Honourable Member’s escape. Their conduct is being assessed and lawful steps may follow,” the Office said. EOCO said the attempted arrest was part of steps it had taken to secure the Manhyia South MP’s attendance in connection with an ongoing investigation. The Office said Mr Baffour Awuah had previously been invited twice in February 2026 to assist with the investigation, but the invitations were not honoured. EOCO said it subsequently took steps to secure his attendance in accordance with the law. The attempted arrest, however, was not completed after the situation escalated and officers assessed that further action could endanger public safety. EOCO said it will review the incident and the available video evidence to determine the appropriate next steps. “The investigation remains active. EOCO will review the incident and the video evidence to guide its next steps,” the statement added.

items.title: En plein scrutin, le Maroc relève son niveau de vigilance après des appels à rejoindre Sebta
items.description: Avant même l’ouverture des bureaux de vote pour les élections législatives du mercredi 23 septembre, les autorités marocaines ont relevé leur niveau de vigilance sécuritaire dans le nord du Royaume. Sur l’axe Tanger-Fnideq et dans les zones jouxtant l’enclave occupée de Sebta, un important dispositif a été déployé en réponse à des appels diffusés sur les réseaux sociaux invitant à une tentative de passage collectif vers la ville. Selon les observations de Hespress , plusieurs points stratégiques menant à Fnideq et aux abords du poste-frontière ont fait l’objet d’un renforcement sécuritaire notable. Les espaces forestiers entourant la zone figurent également parmi les secteurs placés sous surveillance. Les autorités ont mobilisé des éléments des Forces auxiliaires et des services de sécurité, dans le cadre de mesures préventives destinées à renforcer la vigilance et à anticiper toute évolution de la situation. Le dispositif comprend aussi le contrôle de différents itinéraires et secteurs limitrophes, alors que les services concernés poursuivent le suivi des mouvements sur le terrain ainsi que la surveillance des contenus circulant sur les plateformes numériques appelant à un passage collectif vers l’enclave. À la mi-journée, aucun incident n’avait toutefois été signalé. « L’ambiance générale dans les points et axes menant à Fnideq ainsi que dans les zones proches du poste-frontière est calme », a assuré Omar Ayasnine, acteur associatif de la ville. Dans une déclaration à Hespress , il a affirmé qu’« jusqu’à présent, il n’existe aucune tentative d’assaut ni aucun groupe cherchant à pénétrer dans la ville occupée de Sebta », précisant que cette absence de mouvement concernait aussi bien les initiatives individuelles que collectives. Ces mesures interviennent dans un contexte particulier marqué par la circulation de contenus numériques encourageant les internautes à se rendre dans les zones frontalières. Face à ces appels, les autorités ont choisi de renforcer leur présence sur le terrain afin de prévenir d’éventuels rassemblements et toute tentative de migration irrégulière. Sur place, la situation demeure néanmoins normale. La ville de Fnideq et ses environs poursuivent leurs activités habituelles, tandis que les services de sécurité maintiennent leur dispositif de veille afin de préserver l’ordre public et de suivre l’évolution des informations diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux. items.title: El Nino could cause 451,000 extra heat deaths, estimates say
items.description: This year’s powerful El Nino weather pattern could lead to 451,000 additional heat-related deaths worldwide through February as it turbocharges global temperatures, according to projections published on Wednesday. The warming phenomenon, which was declared in June and is due to peak later this year, is on course to be the strongest on record, amplifying the effects of human-induced climate change. The estimates by the Climate Impact Lab at the University of Chicago found that developing countries would be hit hardest by the heat-related toll in the June to February period. The Sahel region in Africa could have an additional 66,800 heat deaths compared to a normal year, with nearly half of that number in Nigeria alone. An additional 19,300 are projected in Indonesia and 19,400 in the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand, and Cambodia. The toll could reach 15,800 in India and 13,300 in Brazil. The researchers projected that global land temperatures will be 1.2C above normal in the coming months due in large part to El Nino, leading to 44 per cent more extremely hot days than in a regular year. For the projections, the Climate Impact Lab used research on the relationship between temperature and excess mortality in 24,378 regions, taking local climate and vulnerability into account. They then combined those findings with long-range temperature forecasts to estimate excess deaths that could result from El Nino compared with the 1996-2025 average. Their method will be published in an upcoming peer-reviewed journal. The report comes a day after the United Nations warned that El Nino represents a significant threat to global health . The Climate Impact Lab researchers said their projections can help governments and humanitarian organisations take preventive measures to protect people, including heat warnings, cooling centres and hydration stations. “This report allows decision-makers to see exactly where emergency actions can be taken now to save tens of thousands of lives in the coming months,” said Climate Impact Lab co-founder Michael Greenstone.

items.title: Manhyia South MP declined two invitations in February, attempted arrest was lawful – EOCO
items.description: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) says its attempted arrest of the Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, on Wednesday, September 23, was part of lawful steps to secure his attendance in connection with an ongoing investigation. The clarification follows a video circulating on social media showing an altercation involving EOCO officers and the MP shortly after he left the Accra High Court premises. In a statement issued on Wednesday, September 23, EOCO said it had previously invited Mr Baffour Awuah on two occasions in February 2026 to assist with its investigation, but the invitations were not honoured. The Office said it subsequently took steps to secure his attendance in accordance with the law, describing Wednesday’s attempted arrest as one of those lawful steps. “EOCO wishes to clarify that its officers, acting in the lawful discharge of their statutory responsibilities, attempted to effect the arrest of Hon. Baffour today, 23 September 2026, in connection with an ongoing investigation,” the statement said. According to EOCO, the attempted arrest was not completed after the situation escalated and officers determined that proceeding could have endangered public safety. “During today’s attempted arrest, the situation escalated, and the arrest was not successfully completed as officers assessed that a counter action would have endangered public safety,” it said. EOCO further acknowledged that Mr Baffour Awuah subsequently went to the precincts of Parliament to seek sanctuary, despite Parliament currently being on recess. The Office said it recognises and respects the constitutional privileges and immunities afforded Members of Parliament and would conduct its operations within the Constitution and applicable laws. It, however, stressed that parliamentary membership does not automatically terminate an investigation or place an individual beyond the reach of the law. “For the avoidance of doubt, Membership of Parliament does not, by itself, bring an investigation to an end or place an individual beyond the reach of the law,” EOCO said. “At the same time, EOCO will not take any step that is inconsistent with parliamentary privilege or any other protection provided by the Constitution,” it added. EOCO, however, maintained that the investigation involving Mr Baffour Awuah remains active. The Office said it would review the circumstances surrounding Wednesday’s incident, including available video evidence, before determining its next steps. “EOCO remains determined to discharge its statutory responsibilities while respecting the Constitution, the rule of law and the institutional privileges of Parliament,” the statement added.

items.title: Bosomtwe Assembly ultilises PWDs fund to empower over 30 PWDs with start-up kits
items.description: The Social Welfare Department of the Bosomtwe District Assembly, through the third tranche of the Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) Fund, has empowered more than 30 PWDs with start-up kits and cash to support their livelihoods and reduce street begging. The Assembly held a ceremony at Jachie to distribute various items, including deep freezers, fufu-pounding machines, industrial sewing machines, laptops and other livelihood support equipment, to selected beneficiaries. District Chief Executive for Bosomtwe, Ing. Abdullah Hamidu, said the initiative demonstrates the government’s commitment to improving the living conditions of persons with disabilities in the district. He said the Assembly would ensure that every person with a disability in the district has the opportunity to benefit from the PWDs Fund. “The Assembly will ensure that every person with a disability in the Bosomtwe District benefits from the PWDs Fund. This will help reduce and eventually eliminate street begging in the district,” he said. Ing. Abdullah Hamidu urged the beneficiaries to make good use of the items and cautioned them against selling the equipment provided to them. “We have given some beneficiaries cash and others equipment. Those who received equipment should use them to establish businesses that will provide them with their daily needs, while those who received cash should invest it wisely in their businesses so that they do not become a burden on others,” he said. Some of the beneficiaries expressed gratitude to the Assembly for consistently utilising the PWDs Fund to improve their livelihoods. “We are grateful to the government and the Assembly for supporting us with these kits. We will not sell them but will use them for their intended purposes. We, however, appeal to the Assembly and the government to provide more support so that those who did not benefit this time can also have the opportunity to do so,” they said.

items.title: Tête-à-tête Doumbouya-Nicusor Dan : ce que les deux Chefs d’Etat se sont dit à New York
items.description: Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, s’est entretenu, mardi 22 septembre 2026 à New York, avec son homologue roumain, Nicușor Dan. La rencontre s’est tenue en marge de la 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies. Selon les informations communiquées par le président roumain à l’issue de l’entretien, les discussions ont notamment porté sur le renforcement de la coopération entre Conakry et Bucarest, alors que les deux pays célèbrent cette année 65 ans de relations diplomatiques. « Nous célébrons 65 ans de relations fondées sur le respect mutuel », a indiqué Nicușor Dan, qui affirme que cette rencontre a permis aux deux parties de réaffirmer leur volonté d’approfondir leur coopération. Plusieurs secteurs ont été évoqués au cours des échanges, notamment l’économie, l’énergie, l’agriculture et la sécurité alimentaire. Les deux chefs d’État ont également abordé leur coopération dans le cadre de la Francophonie. Selon le président roumain, les discussions ont porté sur la vitalité de l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF) ainsi que sur les priorités des deux pays en perspective du prochain Sommet de la Francophonie à Phnom Penh, au Cambodge. Nicușor Dan a qualifié ces échanges de dialogue important pour l’avenir des relations entre les deux pays et pour la stratégie roumaine de renouvellement de ses partenariats avec l’Afrique. La rencontre intervient dans le cadre du séjour de Mamadi Doumbouya à New York. Le chef de l’État guinéen a pris part, mardi, à l’ouverture du débat général de la 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies. Il doit également prononcer, ce mercredi 23 septembre, la déclaration de la Guinée à la tribune de l’ONU.

items.title: Nkrumah’s ideas must be given practical meaning – P.L.O. Lumumba
items.description: Renowned Pan-Africanist and anti-corruption crusader Professor P.L.O. Lumumba has urged Africans to move beyond slogans and monuments and give the ideas of Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah practical meaning. Prof. Lumumba said the 117th anniversary of Nkrumah’s birth should be used not only to praise the former Ghanaian leader, but also to examine whether Africa is making progress towards the ideals he championed. Speaking in an interview with JoyPrime’s Isreal Laryea, Prof. Lumumba said listening to Nkrumah’s daughter, Samia Nkrumah, speak about her father reinforced his belief that the former President’s ideas remained relevant. “When I listened to Samia Nkrumah talk about her father, I knew that Nkrumah is alive and well,” he said. He said people who believed in Nkrumah’s vision had a responsibility to ensure that his ideas were translated into practical action rather than being confined to commemorative events. “It is our duty for those who believe that he had ideas which are implemented to use the occasion of his 117th birthday to remember that he should be given his pride of praise, that his idea should be given practical meaning,” Prof. Lumumba said. Prof. Lumumba cautioned against reducing Nkrumah’s legacy to slogans, speeches and monuments while failing to address fundamental challenges facing African societies. “We can sloganeer all we want, we can erect monuments all we want,” he said. He argued that Nkrumah would instead have challenged Africans to assess their progress in areas such as food security, scientific development, freedom of movement, defence, policy coordination and economic self-reliance. “I believe that the Osagyefo would ask: are you feeding yourselves?” he said. Prof. Lumumba also questioned whether African countries had developed sufficient scientific and technological capacity to improve the quality of life of their people. “Do you have scientific knowledge that can change the quality of Africans?” he asked. The Pan-Africanist further highlighted freedom of movement as an important test of the continent’s progress towards greater integration. “Can Africans move from one corner to the other without hindrance?” he asked. He also raised questions about Africa’s capacity to protect itself and coordinate its policies. “Are you capable of defending yourselves? Do you have one common and coordinated policy?” Prof. Lumumba asked. He said economic self-reliance was equally central to the questions Nkrumah would pose to Africans today. “Do you produce what you consume and consume what you produce?” he asked. Prof. Lumumba said these were among the issues that should form part of contemporary reflections on Nkrumah’s legacy, rather than limiting his commemoration to historical praise. “These are some of the things the Osagyefo will be posing to us,” he said.

items.title: Disproportionate arrests over criticism may create ‘undeserving martyrs’ – Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has cautioned against disproportionate arrests over mere criticism or politically charged commentary, warning that such actions could create “undeserving martyrs” and undermine public confidence in state institutions. The President’s concerns were contained in a letter signed by the Secretary to the President, Dr Callistus Mahama, requesting the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) and the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) to jointly convene a national stakeholder engagement on hate speech, abusive language and harmful content on social media and emerging digital platforms. President Mahama said while hate speech, threats, incitement and other unlawful conduct must be addressed, legitimate criticism, political commentary, satire and dissent should not be criminalised. “The President is particularly concerned that disproportionate arrests over mere criticism or politically charged commentary may be counterproductive, create undeserving martyrs and undermine public confidence in state institutions,” the letter stated. According to him, there is a need for a coherent national roadmap that protects freedom of expression while providing an appropriate and proportionate response to genuinely harmful digital content. The proposed stakeholder engagement is expected to bring together the National Media Commission, Ghana Police Service, civil society organisations, traditional media organisations, religious bodies, content creators, bloggers and influencers. Legal and human-rights experts, representatives of digital platforms, as well as relevant regulatory and security institutions, are also expected to participate. The engagement is expected to examine the adequacy of Ghana’s existing legal and regulatory framework and clarify the distinction between lawful criticism and unlawful speech. It will also consider practical guidelines for law-enforcement agencies, public education, digital literacy, ethical standards for online content creators and accessible complaints and redress mechanisms. items.title: Mir Raza murder case: Judicial commission notes motives of MLO who conducted first postmortem 'appear tainted'
items.description: KARACHI: A judicial commission investigating the circumstances and possible negligence in the Mir Raza Ali murder case has observed that the motives of Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted the first autopsy, “appear tainted”. The body of the 25-year-old businessman was found in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar on July 29, a day after he went missing. After his family accused the police of trying to bury the facts, a judicial commission has been holding regular hearings to probe the circumstances and possible negligence in the murder case. During Tuesday’s hearing, Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed accused MLO Sheikh of instigating a “malicious campaign” against her after she had disputed the findings of Ali’s first post-mortem. According to a written order for the hearing issued on Wednesday, Dr Syed had submitted a “letter coupled with a number of documents as evidence of the malicious campaign launched against her on the instigation” of Dr Sheikh. The one-member commission, headed by Sindh High Court’s (SHC) Justice Omar Sial, noted that Dr Sheikh’s “motives and intentions appear tainted”. “His conduct has attempted to damage the honour of this commission and to detract from and scandalise its real purpose.” Justice Sial wrote that he was saddened to see the police surgeon request the commission “in a very graceful, polite and professional manner” to take notice of the “highly defamatory and dangerous social media campaign against her”. Dr Syed informed the commission that she was under “immense mental anguish and that the material being circulated against her had set a very dangerous precedent that no senior henceforth should attempt to help rectify mistakes done by the junior for fear of prosecution”, the order stated. The commission noted that Dr Syed was a distinguished and seasoned professional with an impressive academic and work background, and her being subjected to such harassment was “unacceptable”. “She is an asset to the government. Rather than appreciate her services, she is being defamed.” Dr Syed had also told the commission at a previous hearing that she faced “threats” after disputing the findings of the first postmortem. In its order, the commission requested the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency’s (NCCIA) Karachi director to investigate the issue of a message exchange between the police surgeon and Dr Sheikh. It also urged the NCCIA to identify whether the defamatory messages circulating on the internet were “forensically satisfactory”, and determine who was responsible for the leakage of these messages on the internet. It directed the NCCIA Karachi director to submit a comprehensive report to the commission before the end of its tenure. During his previous appearance before the commission on Sept 1, the MLO had told the judicial commission that he was not under any influence or pressure while conducting the postmortem and had nowhere stated in his report that Ali had died by suicide. For its part, the commission had expressed dissatisfaction with Dr Sheikh’s answers, questioned the discrepancies between his initial and final reports and asked whether he or a sweeper had conducted the autopsy. He had maintained that he had conducted the procedure and that the final report was issued after the exhumation and second autopsy, following 14 objections by the police surgeon. In a hearing on Monday, the commission also declined the MLO’s request to record a further statement, observing that he “appeared on social media” and said that he had “more to tell the commission than what he told it earlier”. Tuesday’s hearing In its Tuesday hearing, the commission recorded the statements of Abid Farooq Sumar, Asif Farooq Sumar, Faizur Rehman and Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASF) Nida Junaid. The statement of witness Sarim bin Tahir has also been recorded through Zoom. The commission issued notices to Sindh Health Department Secretary Tahir Hussain Sangi, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Samiullah Soomro and Provincial Emergency Operation Centre Secretary Shehryar Memon for their appearance on Thursday at 11am. Memon has recently been appointed as the Sindh health services director general to replace Dr Pervez Ahmed Shaikh — a decision taken by the Sindh government on the day the latter testified before the commission and named Memon as the person who issued instructions to change the medical board formed for exhuming Ali’s body. Notices were also issued to Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) and Investigation Officer (IO) Siraj Ahmed Lashari and CPLC Assistant Chief (Operations/Complaint Resolution Centre) Kashif Iftikhar for their appearance on Sept 28 (Monday) at 11am. According to the order, during Tuesday’s hearing, Ali’s family said they believed another special medical board was being considered. The family did not get any reply upon approaching Deputy Inspector General Amir Farooqi for confirmation. In his order, Justice Sial further observed that if the Ali family’s information was correct, such a move would nullify the commission’s work to date. “The commission will then be unable to give its conclusive findings. It will narrow the commission’s terms. The Government of Sindh has incurred substantial expenses in running this commission,” Justice Sial wrote. The absence of “reliable, efficient, and complete communication” between the deceased’s family and the police was fueling public speculation, the judge noted. The commission requested the Sindh inspector general (IG) that a duly authorised police focal person be appointed to communicate with the family and provide official information to the press and media. The judicial panel noted that the witness statement again revealed that the entire record had not been provided to it. “Even after repeated reminders, such a lack of relevant records is regrettable,” the order said.

items.title: “This is an abuse of power” – Minority slams EOCO over attempted arrest of Manhyia South MP
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has accused the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) of abusing its powers following an attempted arrest of the Manhyia South MP, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, at the court premises. The Minority Caucus raised the concerns at a press briefing on Wednesday, September 23, after EOCO officials allegedly attempted to take the MP into custody shortly after he had represented a client in court. According to the Minority, Mr Awuah was approached by EOCO officials immediately after he exited the courtroom while still within the court premises. The Caucus questioned whether investigative agencies have the authority to enter court premises with the intention of arresting a suspect or accused person. “This matter, I think, should attract the attention of the Honourable Chief Justice. Honourable Baffour is a lawyer by profession. Upon his account, he went to defend his client in court,” the Minority said. “Then just after exiting the courtroom on the court premises, EOCO appears there and lays ambush and makes an attempt to arrest him,” it added. The Minority Leader, Alexander Afenyo-Markin called on the Chief Justice to examine the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine whether such conduct by investigative agencies is permissible within court premises. “I think the justice delivery system – our Chief Justice must look at this, whether or not EOCO or any investigating agency is allowed to enter court premises with the sole aim of accosting a suspect or an accused person. That must be looked at in context,” the Caucus said. He also cited a previous incident involving the former Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, as an example of what it described as similar conduct by EOCO. The Caucus alleged that EOCO had previously attempted to arrest Mr Antwi Boasiako after he was invited by the police. “We are aware that EOCO tried a similar practice, but the police resisted that attempt. When Mr Antwi Bosiako, also known as Chairman Wontumi, was invited by the police, EOCO laid an ambush, but the police exercised high professionalism by denying them access to the police premises,” he said. The Minority Leader alleged that EOCO officials later intercepted Mr Antwi Boasiako after he left the police premises. He described the latest incident involving the Manhyia South MP as an abuse of state power. “What is happening today amounts to abuse of power, weaponising a state institution to undermine, abuse and intimidate a citizen who is a lawyer and a Member of Parliament. It’s most unfortunate,” the Caucus said. Mr Afenyo-Markin said it had listened to Mr Awuah’s account of the incident and was concerned about what it described as an attempt to infringe on his fundamental human rights. “There is no doubt in our mind that EOCO was on a path to abuse his rights, his fundamental human rights of freedom,” he said. He further argued that EOCO could have adopted a more appropriate approach if it intended to arrest the MP. “If indeed EOCO meant well and wanted to act in good faith, they could have adopted some other more humane approach rather than creating the scene,” the Minority Leader added.

items.title: Time to turn Volta Region’s economic potential into action – EXIM Bank CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Ghana EXIM Bank, Sylvester Adinam Mensah, has called for practical steps to turn the Volta Region’s economic potential into businesses, exports and jobs. Speaking at the Volta Economic Forum in Ho on Wednesday, Mr Mensah said discussions about the region’s prospects must now lead to action. According to him, “The time has come to stop describing the Volta Region’s potentials and start building the enterprises that will unlock it.” He said the Volta Region had the resources needed to become a centre for production and exports, provided stakeholders committed themselves to developing viable opportunities. “This region possesses nearly everything required to become a major centre of production, investment and export-led growth,” he noted. Mr Mensah outlined business areas he believed could drive growth in the region and urged participants to work together to move those ideas forward. The forum, held as part of activities marking this year’s yam festival, was organised under the theme “Transforming Potentials into Wealth for the Volta Region”. Mr Mensah said sustained commitment would be needed to translate the region’s strengths into enterprises that create employment and contribute to its development.

items.description: À quelques jours de la rentrée des classes, au titre de l’année académique 2026-2027, le secteur de l’enseignement pré-universitaire et de l’alphabétisation pourrait connaître une rentrée particulièrement difficile si l’Intersyndicale de l’éducation, regroupant notamment le Syndicat national de l’éducation (SNE), le Syndicat libre des enseignants et chercheurs de Guinée (SLECG) et la Fédération syndicale professionnelle de l’éducation (FSPE), n’obtient pas satisfaction sur ses principales revendications. Joint au téléphone ce mercredi 23 septembre, un responsable syndical a indiqué que la rencontre prévue ce jeudi 24 septembre avec le ministère de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique «n’a pas d'enjeu», puisque qu’il semblerait que le ministre soit absent du pays. Selon notre interlocuteur, cette rencontre était attendue «bien avant le point de presse de l’Intersyndicale de l'éducation du lundi dernier», a-t-il expliqué. Pour rappel, l’Intersyndicale de l’éducation porte plusieurs revendications, parmi lesquelles figurent notamment le déblocage des salaires des enseignants, dont certains seraient bloqués depuis 2023 et 2024 ; la régularisation de la situation des enseignants ayant suivi des formations à l’ENI et à l’université en vue d’un changement de grade ; l’engagement des enseignants contractuels, ainsi que la signature du statut particulier de l’éducation… Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Éducation : à la veille de la rencontre avec le ministère de la Fonction publique, un syndicaliste redoute une réunion sans enjeu est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Bring your appointees to order – Afenyo-Markin urges Mahama to act against alleged EOCO abuses
items.description: Minority Leader in Parliament Alexander Afenyo-Markin has appealed to President John Mahama to rein in his appointees and ensure that state institutions exercise their powers within the law. His comments follow a confrontation at the Accra High Court on Wednesday, September 23, involving Manhyia South MP and lawyer Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah and security personnel reportedly linked to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO). Speaking at a press conference, Mr Afenyo-Markin said President Mahama should consider the legacy he is building as he approaches the latter part of his second term. “Not many people get a second chance and I address Mr President as a father who is for all of us. Mr President, reflect on your legacy, you are just two years from exiting office. The question is what would you tell Ghanaians when you are in your quiet moment can you probably say the second opportunity you are given by God you really use that second chance which is rare to transform your country.” He subsequently called on the President to intervene over what he described as excesses by some members of his administration. “Mr President watch these excesses, enough. Bring your appointees to order; call them to order. This is not a Ghana we want Mr President.” Mr Afenyo-Markin stressed that the Minority was not opposed to accountability or the lawful activities of state institutions. “We are not against accountability we always say that we are not against any state institution going about its lawful duty as enshrined in any enactment or the constitution but what we are saying is that a state institution must be seen to be doing its work lawfully.” He specifically criticised EOCO, alleging that the institution had repeatedly overstepped its mandate. Read also: ‘I had to drive off to safety’ – Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah on why he fled after High Court clash “EOCO has gained notoriety for abusing its mandates we all know it but it appears that EOCO is untouchable,” he said. He, however, placed responsibility for the conduct of state institutions ultimately on the President. “But Mr President, in the end it will be your record,” he added. The Minority Leader’s comments come as questions continue to be raised over the treatment of Salomey Baffoe Awiti, who is facing a charge of abetment of crime, to wit publication of false news, in connection with investigations into the “Ghana Jollof” TikTok account. The High Court on Wednesday adjourned her bail application hearing to September 24 after the prosecution requested additional time to respond.

items.title: Mahama tasks MFWA, GJA to lead national dialogue on hate speech, harmful digital content
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has tasked the Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA) and the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) to jointly convene a national stakeholder engagement on hate speech, abusive language and other harmful content on social media and emerging digital platforms. The President said the initiative should help develop a coherent national approach that protects freedom of expression while ensuring that genuinely harmful digital content is addressed appropriately. In a letter dated September 22, 2026, and signed by Secretary to the President, Dr Callistus Mahama, President Mahama noted that Ghana’s media environment has changed significantly, with public discourse increasingly shaped by bloggers, content creators, influencers and individual users of platforms such as TikTok. He said many of these actors command substantial audiences but are not necessarily subject to recognised editorial standards or clear accountability mechanisms. The President described the situation as a “difficult but important public-policy challenge,” stressing that efforts to address hate speech, threats, incitement and other unlawful conduct must not criminalise legitimate criticism, political commentary, satire or dissent. President Mahama also expressed concern about what he described as disproportionate arrests over mere criticism or politically charged commentary. He argued that such arrests could be counterproductive, create “undeserving martyrs” and undermine public confidence in state institutions. “There is, therefore, an urgent need for a coherent national roadmap that protects freedom of expression while providing an appropriate and proportionate response to genuinely harmful digital content,” the letter stated. The proposed stakeholder engagement is expected to bring together the National Media Commission, Ghana Police Service, religious bodies, civil society organisations, traditional media organisations, social media content creators, bloggers and influencers. Legal and human-rights experts, representatives of digital platforms where possible, as well as relevant regulatory and security institutions, are also expected to participate. The discussions are expected to assess the adequacy of Ghana’s existing legal, regulatory and institutional framework, clarify the distinction between lawful criticism and unlawful speech, and develop practical guidelines for law-enforcement agencies. The process will also consider policy, legislative and regulatory measures, as well as public education, media and digital literacy, professional and ethical standards for online content creators and accessible complaints and redress mechanisms. President Mahama further called for alternatives to arrest and prosecution in cases that do not involve threats, incitement, violence or other clearly criminal conduct. The MFWA and GJA have been asked to submit a proposed framework and timetable for the stakeholder engagement, together with recommendations arising from the process, for the President’s consideration. items.title: Staging protests a legal and constitutional right, says KP CM ahead of PTI's Sept 27 long march
items.description: Ahead of the PTI’s planned long march to Islamabad on Sept 27, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said on Wednesday that staging a protest was a legal and constitutional right. Addressing a cabinet meeting in Peshawar, CM Afridi alleged that for the past three to four days, “plainclothes individuals” had been targeting PTI workers, office-bearers and elected representatives. He alleged that an assassination attempt was made on Communications and Works Minister Shakil Khan, who also managed to evade an attempt to abduct him. CM Afridi further alleged that Minister for Public Health Engineering Fazal Shakoor was abducted by plainclothes individuals, who also opened fire on his car. “If a minister, a provincial cabinet member is not safe from these thugs, then what about the common man?” he asked. The chief minister emphasised that the treatment being meted out to provincial cabinet members was “unacceptable”. “These people are afraid of the power of the people. No sane person would take such measures,” he asserted. He also assailed PML-N’s Rana Sanaullah’s reported remarks labelling the people of KP as terrorists and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz remarks regarding the terror threat from other provinces . He said that from today, the province would be cut off from the rest of Pakistan and all routes to it would be closed. “The rest of Pakistan will remain open, but no one will be able to enter or leave KP,” he said. “What should we make of cutting KP off from the rest of Pakistan and closing all routes? Is there a conspiracy underway? Is an attempt being made to repeat the East Pakistan tragedy?” he asked. “Whatever conspiracy is being hatched, and whoever is behind it, our clear message to them is: Pakistan belongs to us,” the chief minister said. He asserted that KP was and will continue to be a part of Pakistan. “Goons dressed in plain clothes are intimidating and threatening our bureaucracy, police, deputy commissioners and district police officers,” he further alleged. The chief minister advised that the bureaucracy, police, deputy commissioners and district police officers to not to be afraid. “If the provincial government is not asking you to do anything wrong, do not obey unlawful orders from any institution or department,” he said. “Protesting is everyone’s legal and constitutional right. We will stage a peaceful protest because we are not being heard anywhere … the Constitution allows us to hold peaceful protests, and we will protest at all cost,” he said. “As long as the right to peaceful protest exists in the Constitution, we will continue to hold peaceful protests,” CM Afridi maintained. “My message to the people of KP and the entire Pakistan is: do not panic, do not be afraid,” he said. Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation are in full swing in light of the potential long march by the PTI and other protests in Islamabad. Earlier this week, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had warned the PTI against its long march, urging the party to refrain from proceeding with the protest. The interior minister vowed the government will not “leave any loopholes” in its response if the party went ahead with the protest.

items.title: Devises : pourquoi le dollar est en hausse face au dinar algérien
items.description: Si l’euro est relativement stable, le dollar connaît une hausse continue depuis quelques jours sur le marché parallèle des devises en Algérie. Les raisons de cette tendance ne sont pas intrinsèques au marché algérien. Elles sont liées à l’évolution du marché international. Au square Port-Saïd, principale place de change parallèle d’Alger, la monnaie unique européenne est échangée ce mercredi 23 septembre pour 276,50 DA, soit un demi-dinar de moins que sa valeur d’il y a dix jours, le 13 septembre. Le billet vert américain a en revanche gagné trois dinars sur la même période, passant de 236,50 DA le 13 septembre à 238 DA le 20 puis à 239,50 DA ce mercredi. Le dollar au plus haut depuis deux mois sur le marché noir des devises La progression du dollar sur le marché algérien a suivi la courbe de sa valeur sur les marchés internationaux, déterminée par la situation géopolitique mondiale et les décisions de la Réserve fédérale des États-Unis (FED). Ce mercredi, la monnaie américaine a atteint son plus haut niveau depuis deux mois. L’euro vaut désormais 1,1420 dollar et la livre sterling est à 1,3305 USD. C’est le plus bas niveau pour ces deux monnaies depuis fin juillet dernier. L’indice dollar, qui mesure la valeur de la monnaie américaine face à six autres devises, a progressé de 0,24 %, à 100,79. Les anticipations de la politique de la FED sont l'un des principaux facteurs qui déterminent la valeur du dollar. Après une première vague de hausses des taux, les marchés anticipent un autre relèvement des taux d’intérêt à court terme de la FED. Plusieurs responsables de la banque centrale américaine n'ont pas exclu cette semaine un nouveau durcissement de la politique monétaire si l’inflation ne ralentit pas rapidement. Quel impact du dollar cher pour l’Algérie ? Les regards restent aussi braqués sur les cours du pétrole, un facteur qui détermine le taux d’inflation. Après une forte hausse la semaine passée, le prix du baril a reculé ces derniers jours mais reste toujours aux alentours de 99/100 dollars. Ce qui devrait maintenir la tendance actuelle des anticipations, estiment les analystes. Pour l'Algérie, un dollar cher est une bonne nouvelle à la fois. Il est synonyme de hausse systématique des recettes d'exportation de gaz et de pétrole, vendues en dollars, et de baisse de la facture des importations puisque l’Union européenne est son principal fournisseur. L’article Devises : pourquoi le dollar est en hausse face au dinar algérien est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Poutine sur les législatives: «L’adversaire a tenté d’entraver et de faire échouer les élections, mais il est impossible d’intimider la Russie»
items.description: Vladimir Poutine a declare ce 23 septembre que les tentatives visant a perturber les elections legislatives n'avaient pas empeche les Russes de se rendre aux urnes. S'exprimant lors d'une reunion avec les membres du gouvernement par visioconference, le president a souligne que les files d'attente devant les bureaux de vote avaient montre qu'« il est impossible d'intimider la Russie ». Les elections a la Douma d'etat se sont deroulees du 18 au 20 septembre. Revenant sur ces trois journees de scrutin, Vladimir Poutine a remercie les citoyens pour leur mobilisation et evoque un nombre « record » de votants. Il a presente cette participation comme un signe de soutien aux efforts engages pour bâtir un pays plus solide. Le chef de l'etat a dans le meme temps affirme que l'adversaire avait cherche a entraver, voire a faire echouer, les elections. « On a essaye de nous entraver, de faire echouer ces elections », a-t-il declare. Il a notamment evoque les tentatives visant a percer les defenses antiaeriennes de Moscou et d'autres regions pendant les journees de vote. Un vote lie au renforcement du pays Vladimir Poutine a ensuite insiste sur la signification qu'il accorde a cette mobilisation. Le nombre eleve de votants temoigne, a-t-il estime, d'un soutien aux efforts menes pour consolider la Russie et traduit egalement les attentes placees dans l'action du gouvernement. Le president a notamment cite la politique monetaire, la politique sociale et les decisions economiques relevant de l'executif. Il a rappele que ces domaines jouent un role direct dans le developpement du pays et dans la capacite de l'etat a remplir ses engagements envers la population. Dans ce contexte, Vladimir Poutine a appele les autorites a « tout faire pour justifier la confiance » exprimee par les electeurs. Il a souligne qu'une politique economique efficace etait necessaire non seulement pour poursuivre les objectifs sociaux et economiques, mais aussi pour affermir les capacites de defense du pays. Le president a ainsi presente le scrutin comme un vote porteur d'attentes concretes. La mobilisation electorale engage desormais, selon lui, le gouvernement a poursuivre le travail sur les principaux axes de developpement et de consolidation de l'etat. « Ce vote est pour vous » Le president russe s'est enfin adresse directement aux militaires engages sur le front. « Ce vote est pour vous », a-t-il declare, affirmant que les citoyens croyaient en leur courage, leur heroïsme et leur fidelite a la Patrie, ainsi qu'en la victoire de la Russie. Vladimir Poutine a relie cette confiance a la mobilisation observee pendant les elections. Il a presente le scrutin comme un signe de soutien aux militaires russes et a ceux qui poursuivent leurs missions dans le cadre de l'operation militaire speciale. S'adressant aux combattants et aux commandants presents sur la ligne de front, le chef de l'etat a insiste sur la confiance que leur accordent, selon lui, les citoyens russes. Il a egalement mis en avant leur courage et leur engagement au service du pays. Vladimir Poutine a enfin assure ne pas douter que les objectifs fixes dans le cadre de l'operation militaire speciale seraient atteints, concluant ainsi son message sur la confiance accordee aux forces russes et sur la poursuite des objectifs annonces par les autorites.

items.title: Avocat : une récolte record de 180 000 tonnes attendue dont une majorité destinée à l'export
items.description: La filière marocaine de l'avocat s'apprête à signer un retour en force marquant cette saison. Portée par des conditions météorologiques favorables et l'entrée en production de nouvelles plantations, la récolte s'annonce record avec des volumes attendus à près de 180.000 tonnes. Les acteurs du secteurs sont très optimistes et assurent que la reprise est lancée. Calibres généreux, volumes d'exportation en nette hausse et dynamique commerciale soutenue, l'équation pour une excellente saison pour la filière de l'avocat affiche des signaux tous au vert. Selon Fresh Plaza, le redressement de la production nationale après une saison en repli est un fait incontesté. « Sur la base du recensement des principales régions productrices d'avocats, de l'augmentation des superficies arrivées à maturité et des conditions météorologiques, je peux affirmer avec certitude que la reprise du secteur est désormais un fait accompli » , a déclaré Ahmed Bouljid, un exportateur d'avocat marocain. Pour expliquer la situation, le producteur a estimé que le stress hydrique n'a pas été un problèmes pour les agriculteurs cette saison en comparaison avec la précédente, ce qui a nettement amélioré les prévisions de production de ce fruit majoritairement destiné à l'export. « Le temps a été favorable aux producteurs cette saison, avec une bonne pluviométrie jusqu'en mars et des températures modérées durant les étapes critiques du développement des fruits. Le stress hydrique n'a pas été un problème cette saison dans la plupart des régions cultivées » , a affimé le producteur et exportateur cité par Fresh Plaza. Grâce à une pluviométrie printanière bénéfique et l'essor des superficies cultivées dans le Gharb, le secteur entre dans une phase de redressement confirmé avec des prévisions d'exportation dépassant les 125 000 tonnes. Selon Boujlid, la production marocaine devrait dépasser le niveau d'une saison moyenne et s'établir à environ 180 000 tonnes, dont au moins 125 000 à 130 000 tonnes seront exportées tout au long de la saison à venir. L'amélioration ne touchera pas seulement la quantité mais aussi la qualité des fruits, selon le professionnel. L'acteur de la filière de l'avocat a souligné que la taille des fruits est en hausse, avec une majorité de calibres moyens et grands (notamment 16 et 18). « Une augmentation du calibre de l'ensemble des fruits est remarquable cette année au Maroc. Dans le secteur de l'avocat, je m'attends à une répartition des calibres d'environ 10 % pour les calibres 12 et 14, de 35 à 40 % pour les calibres 16 et 18, de 20 à 25 % pour le calibre 20, le reste étant destiné aux calibres plus petits » , a-t-il déclaré. Ces prévisions s'expliquent par l'amélioration de la pluviométrie, ainsi que l'entrée en production de jeunes plantations dans la région du Gharb, plantés il y a 3 ou 4 ans et qui ont commencé à donner des fruits. Quant au reste de la saison d'exportation, le professionnel a déclaré: « Nous ne savons pas comment la saison d'exportation se déroulera au-delà du mois de janvier, compte tenu de la féroce concurrence durant cette période et de l'afflux massif de fruits provenant de nos concurrents en Israël et en Amérique latine ». Forte d'une récolte abondante, de calibres généreux et d'une demande européenne toujours soutenue, la production marocaine aura face à elle l'enjeu de la seconde moitié de saison. Elle devra montrer sa capacité du Maroc à maintenir ses positions face à un marché mondial en forte concurrence et presque saturé. The post Avocat : une récolte record de 180 000 tonnes attendue dont une majorité destinée à l'export appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Kpélé/Journée internationale de l’alphabétisation : 17 néo-alphabètes reçoivent leur attestation à Adéta
items.description: Adéta, 23 sept. (ATOP) – Dix-sept néo-alphabètes, formés durant neuf mois, ont reçu, le mardi 22 septembre à Adéta, leur attestation de fin d’apprentissage à l’occasion de la célébration en différé de la Journée internationale de l’alphabétisation. Initiée par l’ONG « Mouvement d’appel au patriotisme » (MAP), cette activité est placée sous le thème : « L’alphabétisation pour les peuples, la planète et la prospérité ». Elle vise à mobiliser les décideurs publics, le secteur privé, les médias et la société civile autour de la lutte contre l’analphabétisme, tout en rappelant le rôle clé de l’éducation non formelle dans le développement socio-économique. La cérémonie a été marquée par des démonstrations de lecture et de calcul effectuées par les récipiendaires. Un sketch axé sur l’importance de la scolarisation et de la formation continue a également meublé la manifestation. Le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Kpélé, Arimou Saboutou, a indiqué que l’alphabétisation ne se limite pas à la maîtrise du calcul ou de l’écriture, mais constitue un puissant levier d’autonomisation, d’inclusion sociale et de réduction de la pauvreté. Il a appelé à la multiplication des centres spécialisés, au renforcement des compétences des encadreurs et à la mobilisation des communautés pour soutenir l’assiduité des apprenants. Le directeur régional des Solidarités, du genre, de la famille et de la protection de l’enfance des Plateaux, Ahé Kokouvi Dodji a fait l’historique de cette journée qui a été instituée en 1965 par l’UNESCO à Téhéran à l’occasion du congrès mondial des ministres de l’éducation sur l’élémination de l’analphabétisme. Il a souligné que cet événement offre l’occasion d’examiner les projets en matière d’alphabétisation puis remercié tous les opérateurs en analphabétisme et éducation non formelle pour les efforts qu’ils fournissent en faveur des néo-alphabètes. Le responsable de l’ONG « Mouvement d’appel au patriotisme » (MAP), Kpatcha Essoyomowe a invité les bénéficiaires à mettre à profit leurs nouvelles connaissances afin de dynamiser leurs activités quotidiennes et d’améliorer leur niveau de vie. items.title: 'Breaking Bad' inspired teenager arrested in Bahawalpur for allegedly attempting to poison father with AI help
items.description: LAHORE: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Wednesday arrested a 17-year-old student from Bahawalpur for allegedly attempting to poison his father, after seeking guidance from artificial intelligence (AI) on how to administer a potentially fatal substance. A spokesperson for the agency said that according to preliminary information, the suspect — a second-year student and the only son of his parents — had reportedly developed strained relations with his father and allegedly planned to kill him following a disagreement. During the investigation, authorities learned that the teenager had developed an interest in chemistry after watching the American crime drama ‘Breaking Bad’. He had reportedly set up a small laboratory at home to conduct chemical experiments, the spokesperson said. The suspect allegedly obtained chemical material from Australia and Islamabad and concocted a substance at home with the intention of poisoning his father. He reportedly administered the substance to his father on one occasion, but the attempt was not successful, the spokesperson said. Subsequently, the teenager allegedly sought further guidance from AI, asking how to administer a poison capable of causing his father’s death without detection, he added. The spokesperson said the Punjab NCCIA received the information about the suspect through an automated system. Following this, NCCIA Punjab Director Hissam Bin Iqbal directed the formation of a team to investigate the matter. The team later conducted an operation in Bahawalpur and arrested the suspect. Further investigation was under way to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident, the nature of the chemicals involved and the suspect’s online activities, the spokesperson said. AI chatbots and agents have been linked to cases of harm and death, leading to concerns about their usage and the imposition of tighter regulations and controls. The Euro­pean Union last month introduced sweeping laws that give it the power to enfo­rce landmark AI rules and to fine any companies that break the law. Pakistan has also previously called for the use of AI to be regulated by the United Nations charter. Last year, American artificial intelligence firm OpenAI said it would add parental controls to its chatbot ChatGPT after an American couple said the system had encouraged their teenage son to kill himself.

items.title: Punjab govt seeks Rangers deployment in Rawalpindi, three other districts until Oct 5
items.description: The Punjab government has requested the federal government to deploy Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali districts from Sept 22 to Oct 5 to assist the provincial police in maintaining law and order amid an expected protest on Sept 27. The request comes as the Kissan Ittehad and PTI have announced long marches and sit-ins in Islamabad in the coming week. PTI has announced a long march on Sept 27 to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan. The letter, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said Rangers had been requested for deployment in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali from Sept 22 to Oct 5. According to a letter sent by the Punjab Home Department to the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control, three companies of the Pakistan Rangers have been sought for deployment in Rawalpindi, including one for Rawalpindi city and two for Taxila. Five Rangers wings have been sought for Attock, while Jhelum and Mianwali have each been allocated one company. The deployment is proposed under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1973, Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, and Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959. The letter said the matter was discussed threadbare at the 59th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Cabinet on Law & Order (SCCLO) of the Punjab government, held on Sept 20. The meeting considered the situational review presented by police authorities, the orders of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in Writ Petition No. 4421/2026, and instructions issued by the S&GAD, Government of Punjab, through a letter dated Sept 19, 2026, it stated. “After due consideration, it was authorised that the requisition be sent to the ministry of interior, for requisition of troops ensuring law and order in the districts mentioned above,” the letter stated. The letter asked the ministry to take further necessary action and intimate the Punjab Home Department accordingly. Section 144 declared Separately, Section 144 has been enforced across Punjab for 13 days, with a complete ban imposed on the assembly, processions, or gathering of five or more people in public places, on highways, or in open spaces across Punjab. Inciting people to unlawful assembly is also prohibited. The ban does not apply, however, to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, or gatherings at mosques and other places of worship. Courts of law, government or semi-governmental organisations’ official duties, and events held with official permission from the deputy commissioner of the concerned district are also exempt. A complete ban has also been imposed on carrying or displaying weapons of any kind in public places, according to an order issued by the Punjab Home Department. This ban exempts personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), intelligence agencies (IAs) and security agencies on official duty. The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said that Section 144 was imposed in view of serious threats to public peace, tranquillity, and the lives and property of citizens across Punjab. “Multiple threat alerts have been received from IAs regarding possible terrorist activities being planned by such hostile agencies by employing suicide bombers, Vehicle-Borne Improvised Explosive Devices (VBIEDs) and target killings during large public gatherings across Punjab to create mayhem, social unrest and disrupt public peace and tranquillity,” it said, noting that “gatherings, rallies, public meetings, sit-ins, processions, and demonstrations” could become potential soft targets for terrorist attacks. The order has been enforced immediately and is to remain in effect for 13 days. In addition, the department also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27 due to the “expected law and order situation”. The letter asked for 2G, 3G and 4G networks to be jammed at specified locations in Rawalpindi city, which it said would be communicated later. It also requested the same for Barahma Bahtar to M-1, Gango, Ahata, Taxila City, Wah Saddar, Thalian, and Chakri. It also requested to downgrade mobile and internet services throughout Attock district. The decision to disrupt mobile and internet signals was made at the request of police to maintain law and order, according to the Home Department. Preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation are in full swing in light of the potential long march by the PTI and other protests in Islamabad. More than 22,000 security personnel led by eight DIGs will be deployed in the federal capital and over 30,000 in the Attock district, which connects Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Punjab. In Aug, the federal government authorised the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army in Rawalpindi for six months to perform “sensitive security duties” and respond to any unforeseen situation. The deployment was approved more than a month before the planned PTI march towards Islamabad. The party claims that the Sept 27 long march could draw around two million participants. District administrations in Punjab have previously sought army assistance under Article 245 during Muharram, election periods, and times of heightened terror alerts. With the deployment approved for an initial period of six months “with immediate effect”, the army units will be placed at the disposal of the Rawalpindi district administration and will perform duties as assigned by the civilian authorities.

items.title: Kozah /commémoration du 40e anniversaire de l’agression du 23 septembre 1986 : Des offices religieux en mémoire des victimes
items.description: Kara, 23 sept. (ATOP) – Des offices religieux ont été célébrés, le mardi 22 septembre dans les préfectures de la région de la Kara, en mémoire des victimes de l’agression terroriste du 23 septembre 1986 au Togo, en prélude aux manifestations marquant le 40 e anniversaire de cet événement. Dans la région, les prières ont été consacrées à la mémoire des victimes de l’agression et à la paix au Togo. Les officiants ont rendu grâce à Dieu pour ses bienfaits envers le pays et imploré sa protection contre les nouvelles formes de terrorisme et de violence. Ils ont également prié pour la cohésion sociale, le vivre-ensemble, les autorités du pays et les forces de défense et de sécurité. Dans la préfecture de la Kozah , la prière musulmane s’est déroulée à la mosquée centrale de Kara sous la direction du secrétaire général de l’Union musulmane de la Kara, Bello Chafiou, en présence de l’imam central. La messe catholique a été célébrée à la paroisse cathédrale Saints-Pierre-et-Paul par le curé Patrice Limdèyou. Au temple de l’Eglise évangélique presbytérienne du Togo (EEPT), le culte a été conduit par le catéchiste Botchona Essozimna. Au cours des célébrations, un hommage particulier a été rendu au général Gnassingbé Eyadèma, présenté comme la première cible de l’agression. Prière musulmane Dans l’Assoli , la messe catholique s’est déroulée à l’église Saint-Thomas-Apôtre de Bafilo, en présence du préfet, le lieutenant-colonel Viagbo Mensah, des maires et de plusieurs autorités locales. La célébration a été présidée par le curé Patrice Morou, qui a invité les fidèles et l’ensemble de la population à prier quotidiennement pour que le Togo soit préservé de toute forme d’agression terroriste. Dans le Bassar , les offices ont été présidés par l’imam El Hadj Batina Aliou, le révérend père Marc Lakassi et le révérend pasteur Moïse Akoué. Ils se sont déroulés en présence du préfet, le lieutenant-colonel Asiah Hodabalo, des maires des quatre communes et d’autres autorités locales. Les responsables religieux ont prié pour les forces de défense et de sécurité afin qu’elles puissent assurer leur mission de protection du territoire national. Dans la Kéran, les offices ont été célébrés à la mosquée du rond-point « Monument aux morts » et à l’église Pentecôte « District de Kantè Barrage ». Le préfet Douti N’Sarma Mabiba, les maires des trois communes et les chefs des services déconcentrés de l’Etat y ont pris part. Le président régional du Conseil chrétien de la Kara, pasteur Yoakal Sambo, et l’imam El Hadj Seydou Zouloukoufoulou ont, pour leur part, appelé les fidèles au respect des valeurs religieuses et de l’autorité, afin de consolider le vivre-ensemble et de préserver la paix et la sécurité. Des offices similaires ont également été observés dans les préfectures de la Binah, de Doufelgou et de Dankpen, autour des mêmes intentions. ATOP/TAL/MG
